Sessions

One handle, one fresh tab, in a browser the engine never owns. open connects — per-call --cdp (your driver skill knows it), else an answering agent-browser daemon, else loopback 9222/9229 — and fails loud naming the fix when nothing answers. close drops the session and closes its tab; the browser itself is never touched.

agent-webmcp open https://example.com# {"handle":"s_…","url":"…","toolCount":0,#  "reapplied":[],"skipped":[]}
bash

toolCount is point-in-time: pages expose tools as they load, so 0 means list again, not give up. Records live under the OS temp sessions dir and are stale-safe — a dead browser surfaces as a transport failure on the next verb, never as a corrupt store. Tabs the browser lost are pruned on the next open; records pinned to an explicit endpoint are left alone.

Every open needs a reachable browser. Every open creates a fresh tab — never adopts an existing one — so parallel sessions never collide. --cdp aims per call; an answering agent-browser daemon is borrowed automatically. No endpoint is stored anywhere — the driver feeds it, discovery finds the rest.

agent-webmcp open --cdp http://127.0.0.1:9222 https://example.com# fresh tab in that browser, closed with the session
bash

Nothing is ever signaled: no kills, no profile removal, no shutdown. The browser is not ours.

Close discipline

agent-webmcp close <handle> --yes   # {closed:[handle]}agent-webmcp close --all --yes      # {closed[], failed[]}
bash

Close drops the record and closes its tab; the browser itself is untouched. --all never aborts on one dead browser; failures land in failed[] with per-handle reasons. Close what you open.
